stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and involves a complex cross-locale (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature. openspec must run first to elaborate requirements, define ACs, and propose technical depth; speckit then hardens with testability criteria, edge cases, and security checks.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a new capability — the existing Stack instantiation in ContentstackFactory omits live_preview config, so the SDK never requests draft/preview content. Enabling it requires passing live_preview configuration to the Stack constructor and reading live-preview URL parameters that the CMS iframe appends. The attachment point is ContentstackFactory; components downstream (useContent, ContentstackLink, etc.) already consume getContentByKey and need no changes — they will automatically receive preview content once the Stack is configured to request it.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array but useful context in notes. I created the full AC list from scratch based on the story title, openspec's notes about ContentstackFactory and live_preview config, and the listed files. Key decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 cover the happy path and backward compatibility — the two most critical observable outcomes. (2) AC-3 ensures the mechanism (URL param extraction) is testable as a behavior. (3) AC-4 covers the malformed-parameter edge case openspec did not address. (4) AC-5 addresses the real-time refresh expectation of live preview. (5) AC-6 validates openspec's claim that downstream consumers need no changes. (6) AC-7 ensures all three codelines (GO, UP, MX) are covered. (7) AC-8 addresses SSR — without this, live preview could work client-side only and fail in Next.js SSR contexts, which would be a common gap. (8) AC-9 ensures preview host is configurable rather than hardcoded (security/deployability). (9) AC-10 covers network error handling during preview fetch. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents. The specific parameter names (live_preview, content_type_uid, entry_uid, etc.) and the exact Stack constructor shape are inferred from Contentstack SDK documentation. If the project uses a different SDK version or custom wrapper, AC-3 and AC-8 may need parameter-name adjustments.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. OpenSpec identified the root cause (ContentstackFactory omits live_preview config in the Stack constructor) and clarified that downstream consumers (useContent, ContentstackLink) need no changes — they will automatically receive preview content once the Stack is configured. Speckit then built comprehensive verification criteria covering the happy path, real-time refresh, draft-vs-published precedence, backward compatibility, SSR, configurable preview host, network error handling, and multi-codeline coverage. The three verification criteria listed in the story are observable and testable. The empty acceptanceCriteria array is expected per brownfield redaction policy and is not flagged. All four declared manifest paths are confirmed to exist across all three codelines (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx) with exact matches — no missing paths. The file set is plausible for this change: the service layer is the primary attachment point, with the interface, component, and hook as supporting consumers. Speckit's caveat about inferred SDK parameter names is a normal open question a competent writer resolves during implementation, not a concrete spec defect.
